page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests placing in the top 25%. The instance demonstrates high memory performance in small-block cached read operations, reaching 4074.06 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average range. Cryptographic and database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by strong scores in Passmark CPU encryption and database tests, alongside a high Redis SET throughput of 63.14 million operations per second. However, large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation speed dropping into the bottom 10% due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

The dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density offer a stable performance profile for multi-threaded workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. This makes the instance highly suitable for enterprise databases, multi-threaded data processing, web serving, and moderate software compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. With 32 physical cores and dedicated CPU allocation, it delivers strong multi-core compute and cryptographic performance, as validated by top-tier stress-ng and Passmark benchmarks. The system lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its efficiency for large-scale LLM text generation. However, it excels in memory-cached operations and database tasks, achieving 63.14 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. This resource configuration provides a balanced, cost-efficient profile for enterprise web serving, database management, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
